study.title: 2 Corinthians 3 The ministry of the new covenant and the transformation by the Spirit
study.overview: In this chapter, Paul responds to the accusations about his apostolic credibility and shows that the very life of the converted Corinthians is his letter of recommendation. From there, he contrasts the old covenant, associated with the condemnation and the transitory glory of the law, with the new covenant, marked by the Spirit, for righteousness and by a permanent glory. The culmination is that believers, without veil, contemplate the glory of the Lord and are progressively transformed into his image by the Spirit.

outline.title: The Living Letter of Christ
outline.explanation: Paul rejects the need for human letters of recommendation and states that the church in Corinth is the visible proof of his ministry. The transformation of believers is described as a letter written by the Spirit of the living God, not in stone, but in the heart.

outline.title: Capacity comes from God and the new ministry comes from the Spirit
outline.explanation: Paul's trust is not born of self-reliance, but from God, who made him able to serve the new covenant. The contrast between letter and Spirit shows that the letter, when separated from God's life-giving action, produces death, while the Spirit gives life.

outline.title: The Superior Glory of the Spirit's Ministry
outline.explanation: Paul compares the old administration linked to Moses with the ministry of the Spirit. If what was provisional has come with glory, then what remains is the ministry of righteousness - has much greater glory.

outline.title: No veil, with freedom and transformation
outline.explanation: Based on the hope of the gospel, ministers speak clearly. In Christ, the veil is removed; where the Spirit of the Lord is there is freedom, and all believers, beholding the glory of the Lord, are transformed from glory to glory.

study.context: The chapter responds to criticism against Paul and also distinguishes the old covenant, given to Moses, from the new covenant in Christ. The given notes point out that there were opponents in Corinth and that Paul uses the very existence of the church as evidence of his mission. The contrast with Moses and the veil serves to show the difference between a revelation that was partial and transitory and the full revelation brought about by Christ.
study.theology: The central theological emphasis is that the true Christian ministry is not validated by external prestige, but by the transforming power of God in the human heart. The new covenant is not only a set of written words; it comes accompanied by the Spirit, which gives life, illuminates and transforms. The law, when used as a means of merit, condemns; the gospel, on the contrary, reveals the righteousness of God in Christ and communicates life. Christian freedom here is not moral autonomy, but liberation from the veil of spiritual blindness and condemnation, for communion with the Lord. The transformation of the believer is progressive and continuous: it reflects the glory contemplated and is conformed to the image of Christ.

scholarViews.insight: The authenticity of Paul's ministry is demonstrated by the transformed Corinthians, not by human letters; the work of Christ appears in the fruit of the Spirit engraved in the heart.
Paul does not want to exalt himself; he acknowledges that the Corinthians themselves are his real recommendation, which shows humility and dependence on God.
The church of Corinth is presented as evident proof of Paul's divine mission, dismissing letters of recommendation.

questions: In what ways have I sought spiritual validation in external signs, rather than observing the real fruit of Christ's work in me?
In which areas of my life I still read the gospel as mere information, without letting the Spirit produce life and transformation?
What does it mean, in a practical way, to live without a veil before the Lord and reflect his glory in daily life?
study.practice: This week, practice two concrete attitudes: first, examine whether your spiritual confidence is supported by personal performance or God's sufficiency; second, take daily time to read the gospel text asking the Spirit to show Christ clearly and transform his character into at least one specific area - speech, purity, humility, or reconciliation. Moreover, value the real evidence of grace in the lives of other believers, rather than measuring everything by appearance or reputation.
study.uncertainty: The given notes do not uniformly detail the historical connection with specific events in Corinth, so the context was summarized only in what appears in the sources. The expression "letra kills, but the Spirit gives life" was treated according to the contrast of the chapter and notes, without expanding beyond what was explicitly indicated. It was not possible to assign to each commentator more than one point, according to the limit requested.
